prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "dalleserver", with the standing line "A small web server that turns any Ethereum address and a chosen series into one annotated image, reporting progress until it exists." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A slip bearing an Ethereum address and a series tag enters at upper left. It passes a checking gate, then forks. A short shortcut arrow runs from the gate to an already finished picture, marked cache hit. The main path winds downward through eight stations in order: setup, base prompts, enhance prompt, image prep, image wait, image download, annotate, completed. Sheets of prompt text peel off at base prompts and enhance prompt. A square image arrives at image download. A watermark is stamped onto it at annotate. All arrows point forward from the address to the finished picture.

Magnified circles set beside it show The first circle shows three identical requests reaching one padlock; one passes, and two turn aside to read progress. The second circle shows the address magnified: 0x followed by hexadecimal characters, measured at 42 characters. The third circle shows an absent key leading to mock mode, with the image step simulated and the raw prompt kept. The row shows five sheets of the same prompt at different lengths.

Colour is used so that Blue marks the request's path through the stations. Red marks the lock and the cache shortcut. Ochre marks the finished annotated picture wherever it appears.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 8 stages along the path, counted beside the stations; 5 prompt texts in the row; 42 characters, drawn as a dimension line across the address; 5 minute default lock, marked on the padlock; 1 annotated PNG for each series and address.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: series on the tag; 0x on the address; setup, base prompts, enhance prompt, image prep, image wait, image download, annotate and completed on their stations; data, title, terse, prompt and enhanced on the five sheets; --lock-ttl on the padlock; cache hit on the shortcut; mock mode on the third circle; annotated PNG on the finished picture; /preview on the gallery wall; /files on the output shelf; ?remove=1 beside a lifted picture; ?generate=1 at the start of the foot timeline; progress JSON, percent and done along the timeline.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: Ethereum address, 0x, series, validate, cache hit, setup, base prompts, enhance prompt, image prep, image wait, image download, annotate, completed. per-key lock, --lock-ttl, one generation, raw prompt. data, title, terse, prompt, enhanced. annotated PNG, /preview, /files, ?remove=1. ?generate=1, progress JSON, percent, done.

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Existing image is served at once; One URL triggers, reports, then returns picture. Duplicate requests only watch the progress; Missing keys switch the server to mock mode. Enhancement off: the raw prompt is used. Removal deletes the image; prompts persist. Poll the same URL until done; Percent estimate learns from earlier runs.
